public_rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. It says that if one of the current stack of AI companies falters and dies, the AI narrative will die, and raising money and selling AI companies will get harder. The contract reads 'current stack' as the major, heavily funded AI companies of late 2025, and 'dies' as shutting down or being liquidated. The evidence does not show such a failure before the evaluation date of October 28, 2026. A June 2026 report said OpenAI closed a $122 billion round at an $852 billion valuation earlier in 2026 (e2). Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 on October 12, 2026 (e1). It said it would keep operating during a sale process that was expected to close in late November or early December. It had stopped training foundation models in 2024. Its court filing put assets and liabilities at $50 million to $100 million (e1). So it is unclear whether this filing meets the condition. The filing also came about two weeks before the evaluation date, which is too soon to see any effect on fundraising or deals. The condition has not been shown to occur, so the forecast cannot be scored yet.
limitations: The first sentence, that these companies depend on venture capital, is not scored separately.
The packet has no AI venture funding or AI M&A data for any period.
Whether Character.AI counts as part of the 'current stack' is a judgment call, and the outcome of its sale process was not known at the evaluation date.
The searches may have missed other failures of AI companies.

our_interpretation: This is scored as a conditional forecast. The antecedent is that one of 'the current stack of AI companies' falters and dies.

In context ('$100 million to $500 million to multiple startups a year', 'AI startups demanding more capital than has ever been raised'), 'current stack' reads as the major, heavily funded AI companies of late 2025, not any small AI startup.
'Dies' reads as ceasing operations or being liquidated, not merely restructuring or a down round.
If the antecedent occurred, the consequent would be tested by a measurable drop in AI startup fundraising and AI M&A after the failure.
criteria.support_condition: A major, heavily funded AI company of the late-2025 'stack' fails and shuts down, and afterward AI startup fundraising and AI company sales measurably fall, with the failure widely seen as breaking the AI narrative.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A major AI company of that stack fails and shuts down, yet AI startup fundraising and AI M&A hold up or grow in the following period.
